meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-07 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Location: Zoom | Recording: Yes
Redwood: Avery Chen (AE), Samir Patel (SE) | BrightCart: Jordan Lee (ML Eng), Priya Nair (Infra Lead), Marcus Holt (PM)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on model tiering strategy (hosted vs dedicated vs cached quantized variants), rollback readiness, canary gating thresholds, and infra requirements. Customer is leaning toward hosted for initial canary with dedicated burst as fallback. Action items assigned around perf heatmaps, KV cache warming, KMS/SSO confirmations, and a 10% canary next week contingent on samples and infra signoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate the time. agenda for today is model tiering, readiness to roll a small canary, and rollback/playbook. we have about 45 minutes.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Yep thanks, Avery. We got a quick update from our side - we ran the baseline on our staging traffic. avg token latency looked... um, between 120 to 220 ms depending on prompt length, but tail spikes at around 600 when we hit cold kv cache.
[00:36] Samir Patel: Okay that's useful. the KV cache cold-start is expected; we can share a warming script that primes common prefixes. also note that quantized 4-bit variants we ran have slightly higher variance on long-form continuation.
[00:55] Priya Nair: sorry, can you repeat the last bit? the - the quantized one, is it safe for us for privacy? we need to ensure no extra telemetry leaves our VPC.
[01:05] Avery Chen: Good call. For private deployments there is no telemetry exfil by default. For hosted mode, we have encryption at rest and in-transit, and we support customer-managed KMS for keys. we'll send the exact KMS integration notes after.
[01:22] Marcus Holt: timeline question: we need to be in pilot in prod with 10% traffic by mid next week — is that realistic?
[01:30] Samir Patel: It's tight but doable if we lock model versions today and you provide the two prompt families and traffic split. biggest risks are warmup and your infra connectivity (SAML/KMS).
[01:45] Jordan Lee: Another risk - our prompts sometimes do long code completions, so we care about token-level cost. how do we balance cost vs latency?
[01:54] Avery Chen: Great question. There are a couple of levers: use a smaller curated model for the cheaper path, or use dynamic routing so high-trust/short prompts go to bigger model, long-form completions go to quantized variant with batch tweaks. plus prefix KV caching reduces repetitive generation cost.
[02:15] [timestamp noise — speaker overlap] Speaker 1: yeah mm-hmm
[02:24] Samir Patel: also, our runtime supports shadow routing and soft-fallbacks. e.g., if your primary model hits a latency SLO threshold we can route to a compatible faster variant automatically, and we can set the circuit-breaker thresholds per-route.
[02:40] Priya Nair: circuit breaker — can that be audited? we need to show in audit logs why traffic moved.
[02:46] Avery Chen: Yes, we log routing decisions and model switch events with timestamps and token counts. logs can be exported to your SIEM; we'll share an example.
[02:56] Jordan Lee: can I see sample logs? the last vendor we worked with had very terse logs and they didn't match our apm.
[03:03] Samir Patel: We'll attach a sample log. it's in JSON lines but some fields can be mapped.
[03:10] Marcus Holt: pricing — if we run dedicated burst for November-level peaks, what are we looking at?
[03:18] Avery Chen: I'll put a ballpark in writing, but dedicated burst pricing depends on committed hours and GPU class. I'll send a few scenarios — monthly commit, on-demand burst, and a blended hosted-dedicated hybrid.
[03:30] Jordan Lee: On rollback — what's the exact short-playbook? we need a clear 'escape hatch' if model quality regressions appear.
[03:37] Samir Patel: Short playbook: 1) detect via our eval monitor or your smoke tests, 2) auto-fallback to pinned previous model version (we keep last n versions), 3) route to shadow-only mode for suspect model while serving on stable variant, 4) rollback and run a quick offline eval. We can automate steps 2-3 with a runbook.
[03:58] Priya Nair: How quick is the rollback? what about KV cache mismatch if we switch to earlier quantized variant?
[04:06] Samir Patel: Rollback is near-instant from routing perspective but cold KV cache for earlier variant may add ~200-500ms for the first few requests. that's why warming scripts and gradual ramp-down are important. We can also keep a shared prefix cache for compatible variants to reduce penalty.
[04:26] [04:30] Jordan Lee: there's a note here, last week's benchmark spreadsheet showed the 8-bit quantized variant had 15% lower token quality on one prompt family - is that still the case?
[04:38] Samir Patel: Good catch. We re-ran the eval with the same seed and saw 7-12% variance across families; that suggests it's prompt-family dependent. we'll add per-prompt family quality deltas to the matrix.
[04:52] Marcus Holt: For canary gating, what metrics should we set? precision/recall-like metrics? latency p95? cost per 1k tokens?
[05:00] Avery Chen: Typical gate includes: functional correctness (manual spot checks + unit evals), latency p95 below your threshold (you said 600ms for tail?), error rate below x%, and cost delta relative to baseline. Also golden prompt pass rate > 98% for the canary.
[05:19] Jordan Lee: our golden pass set is about 120 prompts. we can share 40 core prompts to start for the 10% canary.
[05:26] Priya Nair: SSO — we need an SAML assertion mapping to groups for role-based access. Does Redwood support group mapping to RBAC?
[05:34] Avery Chen: Yes, SAML group mapping is supported; we can map to project-level roles and limit model rollout permissions. we'll send our SSO integration guide.
[05:45] [05:48] Samir Patel: Quick tech deep dive note — when we do multi-variant routing, we track a compatibility score between model versions; the runtime will only route to variants that are API-compatible to avoid schema mismatch with your post-processing.
[06:02] Jordan Lee: what's the compatibility score based on?
[06:05] Samir Patel: It's a combination of tokenizer alignment, output schema checks, and a short semantic embedding distance test across a seed set. it's not perfect, but it reduces breakages.
[06:19] Marcus Holt: For governance, we need an audit trail showing who initiated rollbacks, who changed pinning, etc. is that surfaced?
[06:27] Avery Chen: Yep, RBAC plus audit logs. we can show a sample UI screenshot where you see pin/unpin events and the user who triggered it.
[06:36] Priya Nair: any network egress concerns? if we host, traffic goes over public endpoints. can we run a private endpoint or VPC peering?
[06:45] Samir Patel: We support VPC peering and Private Private endpoints for enterprise. also on-prem package if you need air-gapped.
[06:55] Jordan Lee: oh quick - earlier you mentioned shadow routing. can we keep shadow traffic only for scoring without affecting billing?
[07:02] Samir Patel: Shadow traffic is non-billable by default if you ingest it just for evaluation, but if you store outputs or reprocess in prod pipelines then normal billing may apply; we'll clarify.
[07:18] [07:22] Marcus Holt: I want to make sure our product folks can flip a rollback quickly without needing SE to intervene. can that be delegated?
[07:30] Avery Chen: Yes, via RBAC you can give product a 'rollout manager' role that can change pins and trigger canaries within limits.
[07:39] Jordan Lee: One more question on pinning strategy — do you recommend pinning to exact model sha or to a named channel like 'stable' or 'pinned-1'?
[07:47] Samir Patel: Recommend a hybrid: pin production traffic to an exact model hash for reproducibility, and use named channels for canaries (e.g., 'canary-v2') that map to exact versions under the hood. That way you can audit the hash and still point traffic at a logical channel.
[08:05] Priya Nair: What about degradation — suppose the canary fails quality checks, can we auto-rollback and also quarantine the model to avoid accidental promotion?
[08:14] Samir Patel: Yes, quarantine is supported; the system can mark versions as 'suspended' and prevent re-promotion until manually reviewed.
[08:24] [08:28] Jordan Lee: ok that gives confidence. let's talk about the proposed canary plan. We want 10% production traffic for two days, then 25% for another two days if metrics look good.
[08:38] Avery Chen: Sounds reasonable. I suggest staged ramps: 1% —> 5% —> 10% over a couple hours then hold 48 hours and check gates. If all green, ramp to 25% over a day. we can automate the ramping with rollback triggers.
[08:56] Marcus Holt: Are there limits on the number of pinned versions we can keep?
[09:01] Samir Patel: You can retain as many as you want but we recommend keeping the last 5-10 active versions for quick fallbacks; older ones can be archived.
[09:09] Jordan Lee: On telemetry, we want token-level cost breakdown per request in our billing dashboard. is that available?
[09:16] Avery Chen: Yes, token-level breakdown per request and aggregated cost by route and model is in Redwood Console. We'll share a screenshot and an export.
[09:26] Priya Nair: Any gotchas for EU data residency? we have EU customers and we want tokens to stay in-region.
[09:33] Samir Patel: You can pin deployments to region and we have EU-hosted nodes; if you use dedicated or private, that ensures residency. For hosted multi-region fallbacks we can prefer EU nodes first.
[09:46] [09:50] Jordan Lee: Alright, let's confirm priorities: pre-canary items are - provide 40 core prompts, confirm SAML/KMS mapping, run staging latency test, get the KV-warmup script, and receive pricing scenarios.
[09:59] Avery Chen: Correct. We'll capture those as action items. I'll follow up with the SOC2 summary and the fallback one-pager.
[10:07] Marcus Holt: Any concerns about competitor offerings? VertigoAI pushed a similar auto-fallback feature last quarter — do you see differences?
[10:15] Samir Patel: Similar in concept, but our difference is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and the per-route cost controls. We'll send a short comparison table.
[10:24] Jordan Lee: ok let's wrap — are we scheduling the canary start-of-day Monday?
[10:29] Priya Nair: we prefer Tuesday so infra has Monday to finalize SSO/KMS.
[10:34] Avery Chen: Tuesday works. We'll plan for canary Tuesday 2026-04-13 pending your confirmations.
[10:40] [10:42] Samir Patel: I'll upload the perf heatmap and compatibility matrix by Friday.
[10:46] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll email the notes and next steps. meeting adjourned.
observations: Customer emphasizes tail latency and KV cold-starts as top risk
BrightCart prefers hosted canary initially with hybrid dedicated burst for peak traffic
Quality variance is prompt-family dependent; per-family deltas required
Governance and auditability (RBAC + logs) are must-haves for product team empowerment
